title: Police arrest 1 person, search for another after Seattle festival shooting that killed 3
summary: A shooting at the Bite of Seattle food festival on July 26 killed three and wounded four. Seattle police arrested one suspect and are searching for another; investigators say the shooters fired at each other and there is no ongoing threat. Victims include a toddler and several adults, with some hospitalized.
content:
Updated- July 27, 2026 12:05 pm IST - Seattle

Police officers stand guard at a site after Seattle Police responded to what they described as a shooting with "multiple" victims at Seattle Center, which was hosting a Bite of Seattle food festival, in Seattle, Washington, U.S., July 26, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

Seattle police say one suspect has been arrested and they are searching for another following a shooting on Sunday (July 26, 2026) at a crowded food festival that killed three people.

Assistant Chief Tyrone Davis said detectives don’t have any description on the outstanding suspect. Investigators believe the two were shooting at each other and there is no ongoing threat to the public.

The gunfire erupted around 6 p.m. in the waning hours of the Bite of Seattle, an annual festival that draws hundreds of food and retail vendors and performers.

Three people died and four others were wounded and are in stable condition at a hospital, officials said.

Police earlier urged people to avoid the area just northwest of downtown. A large number of police and emergency crews responded around 6 p.m. and began evacuating the Seattle Center, where the Bite of Seattle was taking place.

Harborview Medical Centre spokesperson Susan Gregg said earlier the hospital admitted four victims including a toddler, a 23-year-old man and two adult women. One patient was in critical condition, she said.

Witnesses described chaotic scenes as crowds fled. Estan Wakonabo said he and his girlfriend were at the festival waiting in line for a photo booth when he was shoved from behind and turned to see a rush of people fleeing.

"People were hiding, were pushing, people were falling on the ground, baby strollers were falling," Mr. Wakonabo said, adding that was when he heard gunshots. "Once I heard a 'pop, pop, pop', that's when I knew it was a shooter."

After escorting his girlfriend to safety, he returned to the scene to take photos and saw multiple victims on the ground.

The annual festival started in 1982 and draws 350,000 attendees over "three days of food, drink, and community celebration," according to its website.

Authorities continue to investigate the circumstances of the shooting, interview witnesses and review video to identify the outstanding suspect. Officials have emphasized there is no active threat to the wider public while the search and investigative work continue.
